Connectome-constrained atrophy in AD and FTD syndromes

Step 1 (data, label checks, parcellation). Step 2 not run: connectomeR 0.2.0 was not supplied

2026-11-21

1 Status

This report covers Step 1 only: data download and checks, label verification, parcellation, coverage and sanity checks. Step 2 (analyses A–E) was not run. Those analyses depend on connectomeR_0.2.0.tar.gz (spin_test(), rotate_parcellation(), rewire_degree(), node_strength(), handle_negative(), and the package that the new R/communication.R should extend). The tarball was not in the working folder, the repository, any branch, or anywhere on disk. I did not rewrite the package from its description, because that would mean inventing code you already have and validated against the BCT.

Two things in Step 1 need your attention:

  1. No DLB map. Neither Zenodo record contains a DLB map, links to one or mentions Lewy body disease. DLB is left out; no other data were substituted.
  2. The three FTD-variant maps have an unusual scale. The NIFD variant maps (bvFTD, svPPA, nfvPPA) span only about ±1.5–2.0, against −16 to +14 for the pooled FTD map from the same cohort. The MINC copies on Zenodo have the same range, so this is not a conversion error. The spatial patterns are anatomically sensible (Section 5), and every planned analysis is scale-invariant (correlations, ranks, weighted neighbour means). So this does not block the analysis, but these values should not be read as t-statistics until the authors confirm what was deposited.

  jsonlite::fromJSON(file.path(paths$zenodo, sprintf("record_%s.json", r))))

  f <- d$files
  f <- f[grepl("Tstat.*\\.nii$", f$key), ]
  data.frame(record = d$doi, file = f$key, md5 = sub("md5:", "", f$checksum))
}))

Atrophy maps. Voxel-wise deformation-based morphometry (DBM) t-maps, patients vs matched controls, on the ICBM152 2009c nonlinear symmetric template.

  • Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.7392621 (Dadar, 2022; CC-BY-4.0): AD and MCI (ADNI), PD (PPMI), pooled FTD (NIFD). The record cites: Dadar M, et al. White matter hyperintensities are associated with grey matter atrophy and cognitive decline in Alzheimer’s disease and frontotemporal dementia. Neurobiol Aging 2022;111:54–63.
  • Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.10383493 (Dadar & Metz, 2023; CC-BY-4.0): bvFTD, svPPA, nfvPPA (filed as pnfaPPA), all NIFD. The record cites Dadar et al. 2022 (above) and Metz A, et al. Brain atrophy and white matter hyperintensities in frontotemporal dementia variants and their impact on cognition. CCNA Partners Forum and Science Days, March 2024 (conference presentation).
  • Neither record has a DLB map or a link to one (dlb_mentioned above is FALSE for both).

Connectomes. HCP group-level structural (SC) and functional (FC) matrices for Schaefer-100/200/400 from the ENIGMA toolbox (Larivière et al., Nat Methods 2021), commit b08974b. Only the data files were read.

Atlas. Schaefer et al. 2018 (Cereb Cortex), 7-network order, FSL MNI152 1 mm volumes and label tables from CBIG, commit 634f676.

scripts/00_get_data.sh reproduces every download and checks the md5 sums.

2.1 Image grids

s1 <- run_step1(write = TRUE)
g <- attr(s1, "grids")
atlas_g <- nifti_grid(file.path(paths$schaefer, "Schaefer2018_400Parcels_7Networks_order_FSLMNI152_1mm.nii.gz"))
grid_tab <- rbind(
  do.call(rbind, lapply(names(g), function(s) data.frame(
    image = paste0(s, " t-map"), template = "ICBM152 2009c nlin sym",
    dim = paste(g[[s]]$dim, collapse = "×"), voxel_mm = paste(g[[s]]$pixdim, collapse = "×"),
    orientation = g[[s]]$orientation, origin_mm = paste(g[[s]]$affine[1:3, 4], collapse = ", ")))),
  data.frame(image = "Schaefer atlas (all k)", template = "FSL MNI152 (nlin 6th gen)",
             dim = paste(atlas_g$dim, collapse = "×"), voxel_mm = paste(atlas_g$pixdim, collapse = "×"),
             orientation = atlas_g$orientation, origin_mm = paste(atlas_g$affine[1:3, 4], collapse = ", ")))

All seven t-maps share one 1 mm grid (all(attr(s1, "same_grid")) = TRUE). The atlas is on a different grid and orientation (LAS vs RAS). It was resampled to the t-map grid by nearest neighbour through world coordinates; the t-maps were not resampled. The resampling code (R/parcellate.R) returns the atlas unchanged when resampled to its own grid, and gives a result identical voxel for voxel to an independent nibabel implementation on the t-map grid (checked during development for Schaefer-400; all 400 labels survive).

The two templates are both “MNI” but not identical (2009c symmetric vs FSL 6th generation). No transform between them was applied; the residual misregistration is a few millimetres, which matters little at parcel level but adds to boundary blurring.

2.3 Connectome matrices

read_mat <- function(type, k) {
  X <- as.matrix(read.csv(file.path(paths$enigma_mat, sprintf("%sMatrix_ctx_schaefer_%d.csv", type, k)), header = FALSE))
  dimnames(X) <- NULL; X
}
mat_tab <- do.call(rbind, lapply(resolutions, function(k) do.call(rbind, lapply(c("struc", "func"), function(ty) {
  X <- read_mat(ty, k); u <- X[upper.tri(X)]
  data.frame(matrix = ifelse(ty == "struc", "SC", "FC"), parcels = k, symmetric = isSymmetric(X),
             diag_zero = all(diag(X) == 0), negative_edges = sum(u < 0), zero_edges = sum(u == 0),
             positive_edges = sum(u > 0), density = round(mean(u != 0), 3),
             min = signif(min(u), 3), max = signif(max(u), 3))
}))))

The SC matrices contain 1, 8, 14 negative edges (unique, upper triangle; twice as many entries in the full matrix) at 100, 200 and 400 parcels. In Step 2 they will be set to 0 with connectomeR::handle_negative(). The FC matrices have no negative values; their minimum is 0, so they appear to have been thresholded upstream.

2.4 Sphere centroids for the spin test

Parcel centroids on the fsaverage5 sphere were computed from the ENIGMA files (surfaces/fsa5_sphere_{lh,rh}.gii, permutation_testing/annot/fsa5_{lh,rh}_schaefer_*.annot; note the annot files are under enigmatoolbox/permutation_testing/, not datasets/permutation_testing/). Because connectomeR/inst/validation/annot_centroids.py was not available, scripts/annot_centroids.py reimplements the usual method (Vasa et al. 2018): the mean of each parcel’s sphere vertices, snapped to the nearest vertex. The snapped vertex was the nearest vertex overall for 400/400 parcels. Compare this file with the package script before Step 2.

3 Parcellation and coverage

Parcel value = mean t over the parcel’s voxels on the t-map grid that have a finite, non-zero t (the maps are 0 outside their brain mask). Coverage = that voxel count divided by the parcel’s voxel count on the t-map grid. Atrophy is defined as −t.

cov400 <- s1[["400"]]$coverage
cov_summary <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(s1), function(k) {
  cv <- s1[[k]]$coverage
  data.frame(parcels = as.integer(k), min_coverage = round(min(cv$coverage_min), 3),
             median_coverage = round(median(cv$coverage_min), 3),
             parcels_below_50pct = sum(!cv$included),
             coverage_identical_across_maps = all(apply(cv[, grep("^coverage_[A-Za-z]", names(cv))], 1, function(r) diff(range(r)) == 0)))
}))

Outputs: data/parcellated_atrophy_schaefer{100,200,400}.csv, one row per parcel, with label, hemisphere, network, CBIG MNI centroid, coverage, an included flag and one atrophy column (−mean t) per syndrome.

The AD map peaks in medial temporal cortex (Limbic_TempPole parcels at y ≈ −20, z ≈ −27, parahippocampal), lateral and anterior temporal cortex, and the precuneus/posterior cingulate (Default_pCunPCC). The bvFTD map peaks in the left anterior insula/frontal operculum (Cont_PFCv_1 at −34, 16, −8; SalVentAttn_FrOperIns), dorsomedial prefrontal/anterior cingulate (Default_PFCdPFCm) and orbitofrontal cortex (Limbic_OFC). Both match the expected patterns. Neither map is sign-flipped or empty.

net_order <- c("Vis", "SomMot", "DorsAttn", "SalVentAttn", "Limbic", "Cont", "Default")
prof <- a400 %>% select(hemi, network, all_of(syn)) %>%
  pivot_longer(all_of(syn), names_to = "syndrome", values_to = "atrophy") %>%
  group_by(syndrome, hemi, network) %>% summarise(atrophy = mean(atrophy, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(network = factor(network, rev(net_order)), syndrome = factor(syndrome, syn))
ggplot(prof, aes(atrophy, network, shape = hemi)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "#a8a79f", linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_point(size = 2.4, colour = col_main, fill = "#fcfcfb", stroke = 0.9) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(LH = 16, RH = 21), name = "Hemisphere") +
  facet_wrap(~syndrome, scales = "free_x", ncol = 4) +
  labs(x = "Mean atrophy (-t)", y = NULL) + theme(legend.position = "bottom")

Mean atrophy (−t) by Schaefer network and hemisphere, Schaefer-400. Each panel has its own x-scale because the FTD-variant maps are on a much smaller scale (see Status).

The svPPA map is most atrophic in the left, then right, limbic network (temporal pole). The nfvPPA map is left-lateralized; at network level it is flat across left limbic, default, salience and dorsal-attention parcels, and its peak parcels are left FEF/premotor, SMA and anterior insula/IFG (table above). The PD map is weak and diffuse. All three fit the clinical syndromes.

  geom_point(colour = col_main, alpha = 0.6, size = 1.6) +
  labs(x = "Pooled FTD atrophy (-t)", y = "bvFTD atrophy (map units)",

The bvFTD map has the same spatial pattern as the pooled FTD map (r = 0.90), but values about 8 times smaller in parcel-level SD (about 10 times in voxel range). One possible reading is that the variant maps are standardized effect sizes or t-values divided by a constant, rather than t-statistics; that is a guess and should be checked with the authors. It does not affect any planned analysis, because all of them use correlations, ranks or weighted averages.

5 Similarity between syndromes (descriptive)

R <- cor(a400[, syn], use = "pairwise.complete.obs")
Rl <- as.data.frame(as.table(R)) %>% setNames(c("a", "b", "r")) %>%
  mutate(a = factor(a, syn), b = factor(b, rev(syn)))
ggplot(Rl, aes(a, b, fill = r)) +
  geom_tile(colour = "#fcfcfb", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.2f", r)), size = 3.2, colour = "#0b0b0b") +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = pal_div[["low"]], mid = pal_div[["mid"]], high = pal_div[["high"]],
                       midpoint = 0, limits = c(-1, 1), name = "Pearson r") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, subtitle = "Schaefer-400. Spin-test p-values pending (need connectomeR::spin_test)") +
  coord_equal() + theme(panel.grid = element_blank())

These are plain Pearson correlations, without inference. AD resembles MCI (r = 0.80) more than any FTD map; the pooled FTD map is closest to bvFTD (0.90) and svPPA (0.77); PD is unrelated to the rest. Spin-test p-values (analysis A) need spin_test() from connectomeR.

6 Step 2: not run

Analyses A (spin-test p-values), B (hub susceptibility), C (network-constrained atrophy with spin and rewiring nulls), D (epicentres) and E (communication models, including the new R/communication.R functions, their bctpy validation and the 0.3.0 version bump) are not run. They need the connectomeR_0.2.0.tar.gz source package. Everything they need is in place:

  • parcellated atrophy at three resolutions (data/), all parcels included;
  • verified label order across atlas, matrices, centroid table and annotation;
  • fsaverage5 sphere centroids (data/sphere_centroids_schaefer*.csv);
  • the SC negative-edge counts to report after handle_negative();
  • CBIG MNI centroids for the Euclidean distances (navigation and distance baseline);
  • bctpy 0.6.1 installed for the validation.

7 Limitations (for the full analysis)

  • Different cohorts and pipelines. AD/MCI come from ADNI, PD from PPMI, and FTD and its variants from NIFD. Scanner, acquisition, age, disease stage and control group all differ between maps, so cohort effects are mixed with disease effects in any between-syndrome comparison. The FTD-variant maps also come from a later deposit with a different value scale.
  • Group-level maps. One map per syndrome means no individual variability and no inference across patients; every test is across parcels.
  • Young-adult connectome. The HCP SC and FC come from healthy adults aged roughly 22–35, not from older adults or patients.
  • Cortex only. The Schaefer parcellation omits the hippocampus, amygdala and subcortex. For AD (hippocampus) and bvFTD and svPPA (amygdala, striatum, thalamus) the likely epicentres sit outside the parcellated cortex; cortical “epicentres” here are at best the cortical entry points.
  • DBM signal. DBM measures local volume change of the deformation, not grey matter. Parcel means near CSF can include ventricular or sulcal expansion (positive t). Mean t within a parcel also depends on the smoothing used upstream.
  • Template mismatch. Atlas (FSL MNI152) and maps (ICBM 2009c sym) are on slightly different MNI templates; no transform was applied.
  • Spin test. The parcel-level spin test can be liberal with smooth maps and reassigns medial-wall parcels unevenly (Markello & Misic 2021, NeuroImage), so degree-preserving rewiring is used as a second null.
  • No DLB. No DLB map exists in the two records, so Lewy body disease cannot be compared.
